route: The upper envelope of monotone rational functions: is the one-player stopping-probability path superpolynomial, and can the tent itinerary drive an all-switches run
object: The upper envelope of the 2^m probability generating functions of the first-passage time to t1 — y^sigma_rho(v) = sum_l P_sigma[tau_{t1}=l | v] rho^l — equivalently the branch of the max-affine eigenproblem lambda x = Lx (lambda = 1/rho) whose parameter sits on the DIAGONAL of the constraint matrix, which is why its optimal basis may return to a basis it has left.
headline: The stopping-probability path is exponentially long ALREADY WITH ONE PLAYER: OF(D), a one-player stopping SSG on N = 9D+6 vertices with m = D+1 Max vertices, has exactly 2^m - 1 = 2^{(N+3)/9} - 1 breakpoints, its path a Hamiltonian Gray walk of the whole Max cube — the fold runs without a Min vertex because |A-B| = 2 max(A,B) - (A+B), the max being a Max vertex and the mean an average vertex over the SAME pair, the minus sign living in the difference of the two options of the next Max vertex; this closes the gap stated at rem:discount-fold and refutes the reason given there for needing two players. With a Chebyshev seed the count is k(2^m - 1) on 9(m-1) + O(k^2) vertices, so Omega(sqrt(n)) 2^m <= B*(n,m) <= (n+1) m 2^m. And the itinerary can NOT drive an all-switches run: the path's switched sets are singletons that repeat 2^d times, which cor:law-u forbids, so no run of any stopping SSG follows the path; a fold block driven by a clock without feedback settles in D+2 rounds because under a fixed strategy the fold linearises to psi_{d+1} = 2 eps_d psi_d - 1.

results.name: ue:onefold — a one-player fold; the stopping-probability path is exponential with one player
results.statement: For D >= 0 let OF(D) be the SSG with non-sinks u1, X0, Y0, F0, H_d (0<=d<D) and P_d, X_d, R_d, S_d, S'_d, S''_d, Y_d, F_d (1<=d<=D), all average except F_0..F_D in Vmax, Vmin empty, edges u1->(t1,t1), X0->(u1,u1), Y0->(t1,t0), F0->(X0,Y0), H_d->(X_d,Y_d), P_d->(F_{d-1},F_{d-1}), X_d->(P_d,t0), R_d->(H_{d-1},H_{d-1}), Y_d->(R_d,S_d), F_d->(X_d,Y_d), S_d->(S'_d,t0), S'_d->(S''_d,t0), S''_d->(S_{d-1},t0) with S_0 := t1. It is acyclic hence stopping, n = 9D+4 non-sinks (N = 9D+6), m = D+1. In OF(D)_rho, with x_d = val(X_d), y_d = val(Y_d), phi_d = x_d - y_d and e_d = (rho/2)(rho^3/8)^d: x_d = (rho^3/2) max(x_{d-1},y_{d-1}), y_d = (rho^3/4)(x_{d-1}+y_{d-1}) + e_d, hence phi_d = (rho^3/4)|phi_{d-1}| - e_d, and psi_d := phi_d/e_d satisfies psi_0 = 2rho-1, psi_d = 2|psi_{d-1}|-1, i.e. psi_d = 2 T^d(rho) - 1 for the tent map T(z)=|2z-1|. Consequently Opt(rho) is a single strategy on each of the 2^{D+1} intervals between consecutive multiples of 2^{-(D+1)}; F_d reverses exactly at the odd multiples of 2^{-(d+1)}; the breakpoint set is exactly {k 2^{-(D+1)} : 1<=k<=2^{D+1}-1}, so B(OF(D)) = 2^{D+1}-1 = 2^m - 1 = 2^{(N+3)/9} - 1; exactly one Max vertex ties at each breakpoint, the level switched at the k-th breakpoint being D - nu_2(k); the 2^m strategies met are pairwise distinct, so the path is a Hamiltonian path of the Max cube each of whose steps flips one coordinate (the reflected binary code); and the single vertex F_D reverses 2^{m-1} times.
results.why_not_implied: prop:discount-fold's BP(D) needs D Min vertices — its fold is thm:fold's device, a Max and a Min vertex reading the same pair — and nothing in it, or in prop:one-vertex-path (which is polynomial, m=1), produces an absolute value with Vmin empty; the mechanism here, |A-B| = 2max(A,B) - (A+B) with the mean taken by an average vertex over the same pair and the sign supplied by the next Max vertex's difference of options, appears nowhere in the paper.
results.argument: The game is acyclic (every edge goes to a sink, a lower level or down the S-chain), so stopping by lem:trapchar and its damped values are a backward induction in which every non-sink contributes a factor rho, a Max vertex the maximum and an average vertex the mean. This gives val(u1)=rho, x_0=rho^2, y_0=rho/2, val(S_d)=(rho^3/8)^d, val(F_d)=rho max(x_d,y_d), val(H_d)=(rho/2)(x_d+y_d), whence x_d = (rho/2)val(P_d) = (rho^3/2)max(x_{d-1},y_{d-1}) and y_d = (rho/2)(val(R_d)+val(S_d)) = (rho^3/4)(x_{d-1}+y_{d-1}) + (rho/2)(rho^3/8)^d. Subtracting and using 2max(a,b)-(a+b)=|a-b| gives phi_d = (rho^3/4)|phi_{d-1}| - e_d; dividing by e_d and using e_{d-1}/e_d = 8/rho^3 gives psi_d = 2|psi_{d-1}|-1, while psi_0 = (rho^2-rho/2)/(rho/2) = 2rho-1. Since 2|2u-1|-1 = 2T(u)-1, induction gives psi_d = 2T^d(rho)-1. By rem:discount-path Opt(rho) is the set of greedy pairs, and F_d prefers X_d iff phi_d >= 0 iff T^d(rho) >= 1/2. T is affine onto [0,1] on each of [0,1/2] and [1/2,1], so inductively T^d is affine onto [0,1] with slope +-2^d on every dyadic interval of length 2^{-d}: T^d(rho)=1/2 has exactly the odd multiples of 2^{-(d+1)} as solutions, each a transversal crossing. If T^d(rho)=1/2 then T^{d+1}(rho)=0 and T^j(rho)=1 for j>=d+2, so the levels' tie sets are disjoint, exactly one coordinate flips at each breakpoint, and the union over d<=D is {k2^{-(D+1)}}. Distinctness of the itineraries is induction on D: two intervals with the same itinerary agree in the zeroth coordinate, hence lie on the same side of 1/2, where T is an affine bijection onto [0,1] carrying them to distinct intervals of length 2^{-D} with the same (D-1)-itinerary. Finally k2^{-(D+1)} is an odd multiple of 2^{-(d+1)} exactly for d = D - nu_2(k), the ruler sequence of the reflected binary code. The multiplier 2 is forced (ue:multiplier in the LaTeX): writing the coefficient of max as A = rho^l 2^{-j}, the X-branch needs l >= j+1, the room for the constant in Y_d's row needs j >= 1, and the constant chain's ratio A/4 needs l >= j+2, so A = rho^3/2 is the cheapest fold, at 9 vertices per level; and z -> c|z|-1 has a compact invariant interval iff c <= 2 while c = 1 is an involution on z<=0, so c = 2 is the only multiplier with growing sign counts.

(i) psi_d = 2T^d(rho)-1 checked at eleven rationals on and off the dyadic grid (1/3, 2/7, 5/11, 7/9, 1/2, 3/8, 13/16, 1/100, 99/100, 41/97, 1234/2027) for D = 0..10, and at three more for D = 11,12,13: zero mismatches. results.name: ue:cheb — a Chebyshev seed: both parameters at once, and a two-sided bound on the envelope complexity
results.statement: Let Tt_k(rho) := T_k(2rho-1) = sum_d A_d rho^d (integer coefficients, from P_0=1, P_1=2rho-1, P_{j+1}=2(2rho-1)P_j - P_{j-1}), let K be least with 2^K >= sum_d |A_d|, and let OFC(D,k) be OF(D) with u1,X0,Y0 replaced by the two lem:dyadic-row gadgets realising x_0 = 2^{-K} sum_d (A_d)_+ rho^{K+d} and y_0 = 2^{-K} sum_d (A_d)_- rho^{K+d} on a shared chain q_l -> (q_{l-1},q_{l-1}), q_0 = t1, of value rho^l, and with the constants supplied by the single halving chain c_j -> (c_{j-1}, t0), c_0 = t1, through Y_d -> (R_d, c_{K-1+3d}). Then OFC(D,k) is a one-player stopping SSG with m = D+1 Max vertices and n <= 9D + O(k^2) non-sinks, psi_0 = Tt_k(rho), psi_d = 2 T^d(u_0) - 1 with u_0 = (1 + Tt_k(rho))/2, and B(OFC(D,k)) = k(2^{D+1}-1) = k(2^m - 1). Hence, writing B*(n,m) for the greatest breakpoint count of a one-player stopping SSG with n non-sinks and m Max vertices, Omega(sqrt(n-9m)) 2^m <= B*(n,m) <= (n+1) m 2^m: the exponential factor 2^m of rem:discount-path's ceiling is attained and its n-factor is needed, the two sides differing by O(m sqrt n).
results.why_not_implied: prop:one-vertex-path realises an arbitrary dyadic breakpoint set at ONE Max vertex and gives only Omega(sqrt(N/log N)) breakpoints in total, polynomial in N and with no dependence on m; it contains no amplification, so it cannot give a lower bound with a 2^m factor, let alone the product of the two.
results.argument: T_k(cos t) = cos kt follows by induction from the recurrence and cos((k+1)t) = 2 cos t cos kt - cos((k-1)t); with 2rho-1 = cos t, Tt_k has |Tt_k| <= 1 on [0,1] and exactly k maximal monotone branches there, each onto [-1,1], so u_0 = (1+Tt_k)/2 has k monotone branches each onto [0,1]. For k >= 1 the polynomial has at least two nonzero coefficients, so every binary digit 2^b of |A_d| has b <= K-1; the corresponding leaf carries probability 2^{-(K-b)} with K-b >= 1 and is redirected into chain position (K+d)-(K-b) = d+b >= 0, so the token reaches t1 after exactly K+d steps, the rows have the displayed values and their masses 2^{-K} sum (A_d)_± are at most 1. By lem:dyadic-row each row costs at most (k+1)K = O(k^2) average vertices, the chains K+k and K-1+3D, and the fold 9 per level; e_0 = (rho/2)^K and phi_0 = e_0 Tt_k(rho). The fold identity of ue:onefold used only the recursions for x_d,y_d and e_d/e_{d-1} = rho^3/8, and (rho/2)val(c_{K-1+3d}) = e_d, so psi_d = 2T^d(u_0)-1 by the same induction. T^d(u) = 1/2 has exactly 2^d solutions, all interior to (0,1) and transversal; each has exactly k preimages under u_0, one on each monotone branch, and each is a transversal crossing (the branch endpoints carry u_0 in {0,1}, not solutions). T^d(u_0) = 1/2 forces T^j(u_0) in {0,1} for j > d, so the levels are disjoint and B = sum_{d<=D} k 2^d = k(2^{D+1}-1). The display follows by taking k = Theta(sqrt n), D = m-1; the upper bound is rem:discount-path.

(i) psi_d = 2T^d(u_0)-1 with u_0 = (Tt_k(rho)+1)/2 verified from the built game at six rationals (1/3, 2/7, 5/11, 7/9, 13/16, 41/97) for every (D,k) with k = 1..6 and D = 0..4: zero mismatches. results.name: ue:path-not-run — no all-switches run follows the stopping-probability path
results.statement: Let G be a stopping SSG whose stopping-probability path visits the Max strategies sigma_0,...,sigma_B (one per constancy interval, in increasing rho) and put Delta_j := sigma_{j-1} xor sigma_j. If two of the Delta_j coincide then (sigma_0,...,sigma_B) is not the strategy sequence of an all-switches run of ANY stopping SSG. In particular: (a) on OF(D) every Delta_j is a singleton {F_d} and {F_d} occurs 2^d times, so for D >= 1 the path is not a run, and the same holds for the Max part of BP(D) for D >= 2; (b) a sequence all of whose steps flip one coordinate is a run only if it has at most m steps, so the tent itinerary — of length 2^m - 1 — is a run only at m = 1; (c) at every fixed rho in (0,1) the sequence val_{sigma_0},...,val_{sigma_B} of OF(D)_rho is not monotone, so the path is not even an improving sequence. Consequently the exponential length of the stopping-probability path transfers to no rule that switches all strictly switchable vertices, and the pivot of rem:blowup-realise cannot be served by making a clock sweep a fold block in the order the path visits it.
results.why_not_implied: cor:law-u is a statement about all-switches runs and says nothing about the stopping-probability path; the bridge is the identification of the path's switched sets — that exactly one Max vertex ties at each breakpoint and that level d ties 2^d times, which is the tent structure of ue:onefold and of prop:discount-fold and is not in cor:law-u; rem:discount-fold merely asserts that prop:discount-fold constrains no improvement rule, and proves nothing about whether the path is a run.
results.argument: By cor:law-u the switched sets S_0,...,S_L of an all-switches run of any stopping SSG are pairwise distinct (with S_L := empty), and if the path were a run its switched sets would be the Delta_j; a repeat contradicts this. For (a), ue:onefold computes the switched sets of OF(D)'s path: exactly one level ties at each breakpoint, level d ties at the 2^d odd multiples of 2^{-(d+1)}, so {F_d} repeats for every d >= 1; for BP(D), prop:discount-fold gives the same count for the Max half. (b) is the singleton case of cor:law-u: there are only m singletons in Vmax. For (c), Opt(rho) is a single strategy on each interval (ue:onefold), so the strategy visited on the interval containing rho is the unique optimal one at rho and every other visited strategy is strictly worse at rho at some vertex; unless rho lies in the last interval that strategy occurs strictly before the end, so the value sequence rises and then falls.

The path's switched sets computed for D = 1..7: all 2^{D+1}-1 steps flip exactly one coordinate, and the number of DISTINCT switched sets is exactly m = D+1 against 2^{D+1}-1 steps (3 steps/2 distinct at D=1, ..., 255 steps/8 distinct at D=7). results.name: ue:linearise + ue:cascade — a frozen strategy linearises the fold; a driven block lengthens no run
results.statement: (i) For any Max strategy sigma of OF(D), with eps_d := +1 if sigma(F_d) = X_d and -1 otherwise and psi^sigma_d := (val_sigma(X_d)-val_sigma(Y_d))/e_d, one has psi^sigma_0 = 2rho-1 and psi^sigma_d = 2 eps_{d-1} psi^sigma_{d-1} - 1, and F_d is strictly switchable at sigma exactly when eps_d != sign(psi^sigma_d): the absolute value of the tent identity is not a feature of the game but of the greedy choice, and under any fixed strategy the cascade is AFFINE. (ii) Hence all-switches on OF(D)_rho — and on the same block with X0,Y0 replaced by any data not read from a controlled vertex — halts within D+2 rounds from every start and every value of that data, level d being at rest from round d+1 on. (iii) In general, let G be a stopping SSG and U a successor-closed vertex set, K := Vmax ∩ U, B := Vmax \ U; then along every all-switches run of G the restriction (sigma_t|_K) is exactly the all-switches run of the sub-game G[U] from sigma_0|_K, and L(G,sigma_0) <= L(G[U],sigma_0|_K) + max_{sigma'} L(G[K := hat sigma_K], sigma'). A block driven by a clock with no edge back into the clock's sub-game therefore lengthens no run by more than its own frozen-drive run length, however many pieces its response map (thm:fold) has.
results.why_not_implied: thm:fold gives the 2^D affine pieces of the response map under OPTIMAL play in the block and says nothing about a run; the linearisation identity psi_{d+1} = 2 eps_d psi_d - 1 under a FIXED strategy — which is what an all-switches round sees — is not in it, and the conclusion that the fold's pieces are invisible to all-switches follows from neither thm:fold nor thm:component-bound alone.
results.argument: (i) val_sigma(F_d) = rho val_sigma(sigma(F_d)) = rho[(x_d+y_d)/2 + (eps_d/2)(x_d-y_d)] with x_d,y_d read at sigma, while val_sigma(H_d) is unchanged; substituting into the computation of ue:onefold gives phi^sigma_d = (rho^3/4) eps_{d-1} phi^sigma_{d-1} - e_d. Strict switchability at F_d is val_sigma(bar sigma(F_d)) > val_sigma(sigma(F_d)), i.e. eps_d phi^sigma_d < 0. (ii) By (i), val_sigma(X_d) and val_sigma(Y_d) depend only on sigma restricted to F_0..F_{d-1}; level 0 reads no controlled vertex, so F_0 is correct from round 1 and never moves again, and inductively once levels < d are fixed, F_d switches at most once more, so level d is at rest from round d+1. (iii) val_sigma restricted to U is computed inside G[U] and depends only on sigma|_K (the closure argument of thm:component-bound's proof), so the strictly switchable set of G meets K in that of G[U] at sigma_t|_K and all-switches on G projects to all-switches on G[U]; the projected run halts after L(G[U],sigma_0|_K) rounds and stays halted, after which the remainder of the run is the all-switches run of G with K frozen.
results.verification: Code /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/296b18c1-9dc5-4a0b-94cf-9bde3946ecfe/scratchpad/r18-one-player-envelope/t_run.py, exact arithmetic. The identity psi^sigma_d = 2 eps_{d-1} psi^sigma_{d-1} - 1 verified at ALL 2^{D+1} strategies and six values of rho (1/3, 2/5, 7/11, 9/16, 3/8, 23/32) for D = 0..6: zero mismatches over 2+4+...+128 = 254 strategies per rho. All-switches on OF(D)_rho from EVERY start and those six rho: longest run 1,1,2,3,3,4,5 at D = 0,...,6, against the proved ceiling D+2 = 2,...,8.

results.name: ue:pgf — the damped family is the family of first-passage generating functions; the one-player envelope is convex
results.statement: For a positional pair pi, y^pi_rho(v) = rho(I - rho Q_pi)^{-1} b_pi |_v = sum_{l>=1} h^{pi,v}_l rho^l with h^{pi,v}_l = P_pi[the token reaches t1 from v in exactly l steps] and sum_l h_l = val_pi(v) <= 1: each y^pi is the probability generating function of the first-passage time to t1. Hence (a) y^pi is absolutely monotone on [0,1) — every derivative nonnegative — so nondecreasing AND convex, with y^pi_0 = 0; (b) it is rational of numerator and denominator degree <= n with positive denominator on [0,1), two of them cross at most 2n times, and two differing at a single controlled vertex v change sign at most n+1 times, only where the single polynomial g_{pi,v} of rem:discount-path does; (c) if Vmin is empty then w_rho = max_sigma y^sigma_rho coordinatewise and simultaneously, so rho -> w_rho(v) is convex and nondecreasing with w_0 = 0 and rho -> w_rho(v)/rho nondecreasing; (d) (c) fails with one Min vertex: on the four-vertex stopping game 0 in Vmin, 0->(1,2), 1->(t1,t0), 2->(3,3), 3->(t1,t1) one has w_rho(0) = rho min(rho/2, rho^2) with w_{2/5}(0) = 8/125, w_{1/2}(0) = 1/8, w_{3/5}(0) = 9/50 and 1/8 > (8/125 + 9/50)/2 = 61/500. Equivalently, for Vmin empty and lambda := 1/rho, the path is the branch of the max-affine eigenproblem lambda x = Lx (L = T read as a max of substochastic affine maps), which for lambda > 1 has exactly one nonnegative solution; the underlying LP min 1^T x s.t. (lambda I - P^{v,a}) x >= q^{v,a} carries the parameter on the DIAGONAL of its constraint matrix, not in its objective or right-hand side — which is why the optimal basis may return to a basis it has left.
results.why_not_implied: rem:discount-path records only that rho -> w_rho is nondecreasing, gives the degree bound and the greedy criterion, and says the path is not the bias homotopy 'because there the parameter moves the right-hand side and here the matrix'; it does not identify y^pi with a first-passage generating function, does not give absolute monotonicity or convexity (which is one-player-specific and fails with one Min vertex), does not give the sharpened n+1 crossing bound for adjacent pairs, and does not put the parameter on the diagonal via lambda = 1/rho.
results.argument: rho(I - rho Q_pi)^{-1} b_pi = sum_k rho^{k+1} Q_pi^k b_pi converges for rho < 1 as Q_pi is substochastic, and (Q_pi^{l-1} b_pi)_v is the probability of reaching t1 from v in exactly l steps; (a) is nonnegativity of the coefficients. In (b), the degrees are Cramer's rule and det(I - rho Q_pi) > 0 is rem:discount-path; for pairs differing only at v, y^{pi_2} - y^{pi_1} = (I - rho Q_{pi_2})^{-1}[rho(Q_{pi_2}-Q_{pi_1})y^{pi_1} + rho(b_{pi_2}-b_{pi_1})], whose bracket vanishes off row v where it is the advantage A_v, and (I - rho Q_{pi_2})^{-1} = sum_k rho^k Q_{pi_2}^k is entrywise nonnegative, so the difference is a nonnegative multiple of A_v at every coordinate and changes sign only where A_v does; over the common denominator A_v = g_{pi_1,v}/det(I - rho Q_{pi_1}) with deg g <= n+1. In (c) the damped game is stopping for rho < 1, so thm:lfp-general supplies one sigma attaining the value at all vertices at once; a pointwise maximum of convex functions is convex, and a convex f with f(0)=0 has f(rho)/rho nondecreasing. (d) is the display. For the last paragraph, L is nonexpansive in the sup norm so rho L is a rho-contraction and lambda x = Lx has the unique solution x = w_{1/lambda}; dividing x_v >= rho(P^{v,a}x + q^{v,a}) by rho gives (lambda I - P^{v,a})x >= q^{v,a}.
results.verification: Code /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/296b18c1-9dc5-4a0b-94cf-9bde3946ecfe/scratchpad/r18-one-player-envelope/t_env.py, exact arithmetic. Convexity: 14000 instances of the convexity inequality (five triples of rationals, all seven vertices) on 400 random seven-vertex one-player games, values computed by solving the damped linear system exactly for the optimal strategy found by brute force over all Max strategies — zero violations. The Min witness of (d) is verified stopping by the trap test and its three values recomputed exactly (8/125, 1/8, 9/50 against chord midpoint 61/500). The generating-function identity checked on 20 random six-vertex one-player games at rho = 1/3 by summing the exact first-passage distribution to 400 steps and comparing with the closed form within the exact tail bound (sum of surviving mass) x rho^400/(1-rho): agreement in every case.

restatements.label: rem:discount-path

gap: There are c > 0 and one-player stopping SSGs with n non-sinks and m Max vertices whose stopping-probability path has at least c n 2^m breakpoints — equivalently, a seed realising an integer polynomial with k simple zeros and k full monotone sweeps of [-1,1] on O(k) average vertices rather than the O(k^2) that lem:dyadic-row costs for the Chebyshev coefficients — which would close the remaining O(m sqrt n) factor between the bound Omega(sqrt n) 2^m of ue:cheb and the ceiling (n+1) m 2^m of rem:discount-path.
next_steps: (1) The pivot, restated with what this route removes. ue:path-not-run closes the tent-driver attack in the form the briefing posed it (a clock sweeping a driven block, in the path's order), and ue:cascade closes the feedback-free driven block outright. What survives is exactly a fold block that FEEDS BACK into its own drive, and ue:linearise says what such a construction must do: along a run the block is one round behind its greedy response and the cascade is affine (psi_{d+1} = 2 eps_d psi_d - 1), so the folding never happens at the strategy the run is at; a family must make the affine cascade, not the folded one, carry the counter. Simulating the abstract system on {+-1}^{D+1} with psi_0 made a function of s_D is one line of code and is the first thing to try. Note that the fold's signal shrinks by rho^3/8 per level while its normalised advantage doubles, so a feedback edge (gain at most one, being a reaching probability) is attenuated by (rho^3/8)^D: a construction must place the loop where the scales match.  (2) OF(D) is the first one-player instance in the paper on which a parametric method is exponential; it should be run against M1-M6, the bias homotopy and R_BR, and its bias-homotopy breakpoint count added to rem:bias-families' table beside BP(D)'s measured 1,2,3,4,5 (the row asked for in the route's item (D) was not attempted here because its first half — a PROOF that the bias homotopy on BP(D) costs at most |C| — was not obtained).  (3) The one-player fold device (max and mean over the same pair; the sign supplied by the next Max vertex's difference of options) is not tied to the damping parameter: the same three lines turn thm:fold's response map, prop:leapfrog's per-vertex switch counts and any other place the paper spends a Min vertex on an absolute value into one-player constructions. thm:fold's P_D with D Min vertices is the obvious first target — a one-player game whose freeze response map has 2^D pieces would strengthen sec:fold and rem:fold-width.  (4) The gap field: an O(k) seed. A Horner-style chain realising sum_d A_d rho^d with A_d of Theta(k) bits, or a different polynomial family with sparse integer coefficients and k full sweeps, would give B*(n,m) = Omega(n 2^m) and leave only the factor m.  (5) ue:multiplier says the tent is the only fold a substochastic calculus can run (c <= 2 for an invariant interval, c a power of two, c = 1 an involution), so 2^m is the exact ceiling of this shape; whether some other shape — several Max vertices per level, or a block that is not levelled — beats it is open and is the same question as (4) from the other side.
prior_art: From memory, unchecked against the sources. (i) Chebyshev polynomials: T_k(cos t) = cos kt, the recurrence and the k+1 equioscillations on [-1,1] — classical; used here only through the recurrence, which is proved inline. (ii) The tent map, its symbolic dynamics and the fact that its itinerary is the reflected binary (Gray) code — classical (Milnor-Thurston kneading theory); the paper already uses the tent map at thm:fold and prop:discount-fold and the itinerary claim is proved here from scratch. (iii) Probability generating functions of first-passage times and absolute monotonicity — classical (Feller). (iv) The upper envelope of functions pairwise crossing at most s times has Davenport-Schinzel complexity lambda_s(N) (Hart-Sharir, Agarwal-Sharir); it is NOT used, because lambda_{2n}(2^m) is far worse here than the paper's own greedy-criterion bound (n+1)m2^m. (v) The policy-difference identity used in ue:pgf(b) is the standard policy-improvement/advantage identity of dynamic programming (Howard, Blackwell); the paper has it as thm:impedance. (vi) The sensitive-discount / Blackwell-optimality reading of a breakpoint is already attributed at rem:discount-fold (Blackwell, Veinott, Miller-Veinott). (vii) d'Epenoux's occupancy LP and the shadow-vertex reading are the paper's prop:oneplayer-lp and prop:bias-shadow. (viii) Melekopoglou-Condon remains the one-player half of the pivot; nothing here bears on it, since ue:path-not-run separates the parametric path from the run. No web access was used.
